sentences.text:
Applicant has filed this first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.371/2023 registered at P.S. Sanyogitaganj, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
2.

As per the prosecution story, IDA executed a lease deed dated 14.05.1999 in favour of the Bombay Builders Private Limited and on 07.10.1997 an agreement to sale for shop No.26 to the tune of Smt. 1 Rs.12,18,850/- was executed between the Nandkishore (father-in-law of the present applicant) and the Company, but Nandkishore failed to pay the consideration amount and after the death of Nandkishore in September, 2018 complainant requested the Sanjay (husband of the applicant) to vacate the subject shop, but subject shop was not vacated.

entities.text: Aruna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant is not registered owner of the subject shop, but present applicant with dishonest intention fraudulently executed registered lease deed dated 20.10.2022 for the subject shop in favour Sandeep Goyal by mentioning that she is the owner of possession holder of the subject shop situated at Hardeep Tower.
Then complainant made a complaint before P.S. Sanyogitaganj, Indore.

On 22.10.2022, respondent submitted a report under Section 145 of Cr.P.C. before the learned SDO, Bicholi, Hapsi, Indore, and thereafter receiver was appointed in February, 2023 then applicant filed a civil suit for specific performance of the agreement dated 07.10.1997 before the Civil Court.
Accordingly, offence has been registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent person and she has been falsely implicated in this matter.

Shop Nos. 26, 26-A, 27 and 32 were sold by the Director Harvinder Singh Hora to one Nandkishore through agreement dated 09.01.1997 and the possession of Shop No.26 was given on 07.10.1997 on payment of Rs.7,14,096/- through various cheques.

Nandkishore has been died on 15.04.2018 and before his death, he executed Will regarding the suit shop in favour of the applicant and for the change of ownership applicant has filed proceedings for probate and succession certificate before the competent Court, which is still pending.

Husband of the applicant has died on 03.03.2023 and after 10 days brother of complainant Harshdeep Singh Hora pressurized the applicant to handover the shop in his favour then she made a complaint before the Police.
Order passed by the SDM, Indore, division was decided by the XIXth ASJ, Indore on 08.08.2023.
The present case is of civil nature.
Applicant is a young lady of 34 years of age and is permanent resident of District Indore and there is no possibility of her absconding.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that the applicant be released on anticipatory bail.
4. Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

5. Learned counsel for objector also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that Nandkishore has not filed any suit for specific performance of agreement dated 07.10.1997.
The civil suit has been filed after a lapse of 25 years.
Applicant has fraudulently created false, forged and fabricated documents with a sole motive to create her legal rights over the subject shops.
Subject shops were never sold by the complainant to Nandkishore Tiwari.
Applicant has two more criminal antecedents of similar nature.
Hence, she does not deserve for bail.

6. Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order passed by the court below.
7. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature and gravity of allegation and also taking note of the fact that present applicant is not the registered owner of the shops in question.
She has executed rent agreement in favour of her husband Sanjay Tiwari by stating that she is the owner of the suit shop.

9. Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail application preferred under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.
With the aforesaid, the application stands disposed off.
